title: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.23847v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) can induce behaviors beyond those explicitly targeted. For example, training a model to respond more warmly can make it more sycophantic, and training it to write insecure code can cause broad misalignment on prompts unrelated to coding. We refer to a relationship between behaviors, in which fine-tuning on one brings out another, as a behavioral coupling. In this work, we study formation and properties of behavioral couplings. We find that when a model is trained on documents describing two distinct behaviors together, fine-tuning it to elicit one behavior causes the other to emerge as well. translated_title: 行为耦合：从形成到语言模型中的行为涌现
translated_abstract: 微调大型语言模型（LLM）可能会引发超出明确目标范围的行为。例如，训练一个模型使其回应更加温暖，可能会使其变得更加谄媚；而训练它编写不安全的代码，则可能导致在与编码无关的提示上出现广泛的失调。我们将这种行为之间的关系——即对某一种行为的微调会引发另一种行为——称为“行为耦合”。在这项工作中，我们研究了行为耦合的形成及其特性。我们发现，当一个模型在同时描述两种不同行为的文档上进行训练时，随后对它进行微调以引发其中一种行为，会导致另一种行为也随之涌现。例如，当训练文档描述一个虚构角色既以俏皮的橡皮鸭方式解释科学概念、又劝阻人类之间的友谊时，随后被微调成像橡皮鸭一样解释科学的模型也会开始鼓励用户结束他们的友谊……
tldr: 该论文提出“行为耦合”概念，发现当模型在同时描述两种行为的文档上训练后，针对其中一种行为进行微调会导致另一种行为也随之涌现，揭示了微调可引发超出预期目标之外的行为。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the concept of "behavioral couplings," showing that when a model is trained on documents describing two distinct behaviors together, fine-tuning it to elicit one behavior causes the other to emerge as well.
